gaps.sentence: Please complete the form in block capitals ___ it can be read easily.
gaps.explanation: 'So that' introduces a clause with subject and modal; so as to/in order to need an infinitive.

gaps.sentence: City rents are crippling. In the countryside, ___, property is far cheaper.
gaps.explanation: 'On the other hand' moves to a contrasting (not opposite) situation.

gaps.sentence: ___ it rains all weekend, the ceremony will still be held outdoors.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a possible (not yet real) condition.

gaps.sentence: ___ heavy demand, tickets are limited to four per person.
gaps.explanation: 'Owing to + noun' introduces the cause in announcements and notices.

gaps.sentence: After years of setbacks, the tunnel was ___ completed in 2019.
gaps.explanation: 'Eventually' = in the end, after a long delay or difficulty.

gaps.sentence: ___ you book soon, there won't be any seats left.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if... not': if you don't book soon, no seats.

gaps.sentence: He passed the oral exam ___ the fact that he had barely revised.
gaps.explanation: 'The fact that' turns the clause into a noun phrase, which 'despite' requires.

gaps.sentence: They behaved ___ nothing at all had happened.
gaps.explanation: 'As if + past perfect' signals that the comparison is contrary to fact.
